reviews.decision_reason: select_demand selects records using only demand_score threshold and fallback IDs. The supplied corpus contains need text, scores, source IDs, and source weights, but no observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes. Under the strict market-demand criteria, this cannot establish customer demand, so the unit admits unsupported candidates into the demand set.

normalize truncates the selected demand set to a one-row fixed window. That preserves only n06-r01 and drops the other supplied needs before downstream coverage, so missing or contradictory demand evidence cannot remain visible. The unit also does not validate the strict demand criteria; it only filters record IDs and keeps the first row.

assemble_provenance ranks whatever rows it receives and carries source_id/source_weight, but those fields are not sufficient market-demand evidence. The direct behavioral truncation is upstream in normalize, yet this unit still converts unsupported rows into provenance-looking evidence sources without preserving observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes.
